 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19-04-2023.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 19-04-2023 at about 8.00 a.m., the petitioner was riding his vehicle on the left side of the road near Lotus Hospital, 24th main road, HSR Layout, Bengaluru, and at that time the driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318 drove the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner' vehicle from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Lotus Hospital,
thereafter shifted to Narayana Multi-speciality Hospital, Bengaluru wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.

The petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, conveyance, medical treatment,
attendant and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 55 years, hale and healthy and was doing Business and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of summons, respondents have appeared through their counsels, but the respondent No.1 -owner failed to file written statement.
The respondent No.2- insurer has filed written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident.

Further it has admitted the issuance of policy to the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318 which was in force as on the date of accident and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further this respondent submits that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence so also the offending vehicle had no valid RC and FC, therefore the same is violation of motor vehicle act.
Further it has also denied the age, occupation, income and injuries sustained by the petitioner and also the treatment taken for the injuries.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

2.

On the other hand, the respondents did not choose to led any rebuttal evidence.

8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, Statement of victim, IMV notice and reply, police intimation and charge sheet, all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.10.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of first information given by one Smt. Tulasi S.
who is the wife of the petitioner by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar were conducted.
On perusal of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, the accident spot is in left side of the road where the accident spot is within 10 feet from the footpath.
It is alleged that the offending vehicle bearing MP-20-CL-7318 came from backside of the motorcycle of the petitioner and dashed against the rear side of the motorcycle of the petitioner.
10. The Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein the motorcycle of the petitioner has got damages in its front crash guard, rear right side indicator damaged.
On the other hand the offending car bearing No. MP-20-CL-7318 has got damages in its left hand side both door (Front & rear) damaged.

The respondent No.1 being the owner not examined his driver by denying the negligence of the driver of the car.

11. Ex.P10 charge sheet is also came to be filed on against the driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318, and the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.1 -owner even though appeared neither filed written statement nor produced any document in support of his case.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability but not produced any documents in support of its case.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318.
13.
The alleged accident is of dated 19-04-2023 but the FIR was registered on 02-05-2023 i.e., after 15 days of accident.

In this regard petitioner produced Ex.P9 Police intimation and Ex.P.11 discharge summary where it evidentiates that on 19.04.2023 itself the petitioner admitted to Narayana Multi Speciality hospital at 9.00 a.m. with a history of RTA.
As per Ex.P.9 police intimation the accident between 2 wheeler and 4 wheeler.
Thus as per Ex.P.2 the petitioner assigned reasons for delay in lodging the complaint that driver of the offending car assured that he will bear the hospital expenditure.
Thereby the delay of 15 days in filing the complaint is explained by the petitioner by producing Ex.P.9 police intimation.
14. The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the the driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL-7318 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC.

16. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by denying their liability and alleged negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
17. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, Ex.P4 IMV report helped the petitioner to prove his case.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 10 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 19-04-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP- 20-CL-7318 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
20. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P5 which shows that the petitioner sustained Rib fracture 3rd to 6th.
Even though the petitioner examined Dr.N. Sridhar, Orthopedic Consultant at Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, Bengaluru but he has assessed disability.
Without the assessing the disability by the doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained permanent disability due to grievous injuries.
21. According to the petitioner he was doing business and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
But to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

22. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and Srinivas Reddy M vs Sunil Sarma on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66608677/
5 enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.5 - wound certificate and Ex.P11 discharge summary, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injury.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner was admitted to Narayana Multispeciality Hospital on 19-04-2023 and discharged on 22-04-2023.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs. 40,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills which is marked as Ex.P-13 amounting to Rs.1,18,515/-.
These bills are supported with the prescriptions marked at Ex.P14.

On perusal of these bills the bill at Sl. No.1 i.e., inpatient bill amounting to Rs.33,588/-
out of which Rs.14,763/- was paid by the Medi Assist India Private Limited.
Hence after deducting the same Rs.16,186/- taken for consideration.
The Sl. No.4 and 11 bills in Ex.P.13 has no description for what purpose the said was paid.
The said bill looks like an advance bill, hence the same cannot be considered.

The Sl. No.3 bill is a copy of the bill which has no seal and signature, but the said bill is computer generated bill hence only on the ground of not having the seal and signature it cannot be rejected.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the bills produced at Ex.P.13 except the Sl. No.4 and 11.
Thereby the total amount of remaining bill is of Rs.69,753/- by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.70,000/- is awarded under this head.
(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed the discharge summary Ex.P-11, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent conservative treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated Srinivas Reddy M vs Sunil Sarma on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66608677/
6 him.

entities.text: Srinivas Reddy M vs Sunil Sarma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his income and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period hence, in the absence of any evidence,
petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
Future Medical Expenses:
The petitioner by claiming future medical expenses examined one Dr. N. Sridhar as PW2.

The PW2 in his evidence affidavit stated that he clinically examined the petitioner and found that the rib fractures are healed, but there is a right shoulder stiffness and painful and the recent ultra sound scan for right shoulder shows the Calcific tendinities with shoulder stiffness and for the same the petitioner has to undergo Acthroscopic Robotic repair and post surgery needs to go physiotherapy which may cost upto Rs.2,00,000/- to Rs.2,50,000/-.
In this regard when the PW2 was cross-examined once again the PW2 stated that the fractures are united and lungs are also cleared and also stated that he has not given detailed estimation.

Further in the cross-examination he has answered that they have advised PRP injection for the problems and if the said problems are not cleared by the said injection then there is a need of Acthroscopic Robotic repair.
As per the answers given by the PW2 the said PRP injection may cost upto Rs.15,000/-.

Thereby, if we consider the evidence of PW2 doctor even though he stated that Acthroscopic Robotic repair may cost upto Rs.2,00,000/-to Rs.2,50,000/- he has not produced any detailed break up estimation.
Further the fractures was at 3rd and 6th rib.
Further Calcific tendinitis is a condition where calcium deposits form in the shoulder's rotator cuff tendons, causing intense pain, stiffness, and reduced range of motion.

Thereby the petitioner not produced any evidence and the evidence of the PW2 doctor is also not clear to show that the fracture of 3rd and 6th rib has the direct nexus with Calcific tendinitis in the right shoulder.

As per the evidence of PW2 doctor Srinivas Reddy M vs Sunil Sarma on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66608677/
7

sentences.text: the said Calcific tendinitis can be cleared with PRP injection also.
In the absence of proper evidence in this regard Rs.30,000/- awarded under this head.

22. To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following A) Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000-00 B) Towards Medical expenses Rs. 70,000-00 C) Towards diet, food, nourishment, Rs. 20,000-00 attendant and conveyance charges D) Towards loss of future earning NIL capacity E)
Loss of income during laid up NIL period F) Towards loss of amenities Rs.
20,000-00 G) Future Medical Expenses Rs.30,000-00 Total Rs. 1,80,000-00 23. Liability:-

The respondent No. 2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending Maruthi Wagnor Car bearing No.MP-20-CL- 7318 and taken contention that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid licence at the time of accident.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
24. ISSUE NO.3:
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,80,000/- (Rupees One lakh eighty thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 - insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
